notes: Makes buttermilk, rava idli and dosa batter from scratch.

person_rules.note: Neeru does not eat garam masala at all - OMIT and use black pepper instead. Modelled as an omit/substitute instruction (many repo recipes list it) rather than a dish exclusion.
Not fond of paneer or cheese - limited quantity; paneer sourced from the local Greenage vendor.
Diabetic - avoid sugary fruits (banana/chikku) in smoothies and snacks.
French beans not preferred - minimal quantity if used.

dish_keyword_rules.note: Diabetic-safe: no high-sugar fruit or sweeteners in smoothies/snacks (Neeru).
Household does NOT eat roti-sabji for dinner as a norm - dinner is light (soup, rolls, cutlet).

frequency_caps.name: Paneer
frequency_caps.note: Neeru not fond of paneer - limited use.

brand_rules.note: Paneer from the local vendor, not grocery apps.

ingredient_grade_rules.rule: Never use - black pepper is the substitute.
White urad dal only - black urad dal is an allergy risk.
Regular tomatoes only, never cherry tomatoes; onions and tomatoes always well cooked, never kaccha (gastric health).
Generous ginger-garlic everywhere, especially legumes (black chana, kabuli chana, rajma, kadhi) - insufficient garlic caused day-long digestion trouble.
Soak one day, eat the next; never serve stale/spoiled sprouts.
Hard-boiled preferred; omelette well-done, cooked both sides.
Used sparingly - one stock lasts months; restock only when depleted.
Welcome as rice substitute (pulao / bisi bele bath style) but low-prep methods only.
Salty variant with curd + tadka, not sweet.

breakfast_style: Egg white omelette (well-done), sprouted moong, ragi roti, millet dosa, rava idli (fresh batter), salty ragi malt; legumes with generous garlic in the morning.

cooking_technique.seasoning: Low oil, low spice, mild/normal salt as the default for every dish
cooking_technique.onion_tomato: Always well cooked, never kaccha - gastric health, not taste
cooking_technique.portions: Smaller than restaurant portions - 'quantity should be very less, we are not able to finish'; 2 rotis per person per meal
cooking_technique.dinner: Light meal (soup, rolls, cutlet) - not roti-sabji
cooking_technique.batters: Buttermilk, rava idli and dosa batter from scratch - never ready-made
cooking_technique.regional_rotation: Bihar, Rajasthan, Punjab, South Indian dishes weekly as sabzi/starter

nutrition_direction: Diabetic-safe: minimise simple carbs (pasta/pizza/burgers, sugary fruit), favour complex carbs and millets
Iron-rich, nutrient-dense meals (anemia, B12/D deficiency) - e.g. spinach
High fibre / protein: egg whites, sprouts, legumes with garlic
Everything cooked properly - technique over variety
weekend_pattern: Saturday shifts at 8:00-8:30 AM and 6:00 PM; Sunday off.
standing_instructions: Low oil, low spice, mild/normal salt in every dish; generous ginger-garlic; onions/tomatoes fully cooked.
2 rotis per person per meal; batch sizes smaller than standard.
Dinner is light (soup / cutlet / rolls) - not roti-sabji.
Buttermilk and batters made fresh in-house.
Cut salad (carrot, cucumber) and cut fruit prepared daily by default, without being asked.
Sprouts fresh-soaked (1-day cycle); discard if stale.
Dal restocked only when depleted; paneer from Greenage vendor.
Garam masala never (black pepper); maida never; cream never (fresh milk); black urad dal never; mushroom never; cherry tomatoes never.
Diabetic snacking: no banana/chikku or high-sugar fruit in smoothies/snacks.
Weekly regional rotation (Bihar, Rajasthan, Punjab, South Indian).
Kitchen managed solely by Neeru - cook has no ordering authority.
Injury: report immediately, first-aid box - never self-treat.
non_negotiables: Never use cream - fresh milk only.
Never use black urad dal - white only.
Never skip the daily salad/cut-fruit prep.
Never let onions/tomatoes go into a dish kaccha.
notes: 'Household does not eat chicken' is a low-confidence inferred rule that conflicts with Licious orders on file - chicken is excluded here until confirmed.
